messages:
Anya: Hey team, kicking off a canary for palomino12b (v1-int4) on pool-42. Observed intermittent OOMs during long generations and a small quality drop on summarization eval (~2.1 ROUGE pts). Logs show: `OOM: alloc failed at kv_cache_allocate`
Dmitri: Which runtime config are you using? prefetch enabled? continuous batching? max_new_tokens?
Anya: prefetch=true, continuous batching, microbatch=8, slot_reserve=0.05, max_new_tokens=256 (default). Repro is long-prompt test -> ~1k generated tokens. OOMs tend to happen ~700 tokens in.
Lucas: Two quick experiments: 1) disable prefetch and lower max_new_tokens to 128; 2) keep prefetch but set slot_compactor_threshold higher (0.12). Which is easier to try on canary?
Anya: Trying option 1 first. Triggering a canary run with `curl -X POST https://canary/api/serve -d '{"model":"palomino12b-int4","options":{"max_new_tokens":128,"prefetch":false}}'` (job 4832123462).
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for palomino12b-int4 on pool-42 (job 4832123462).
Dmitri: If you can, capture `nvidia-smi` and the driver allocator log at OOM time. My hypothesis is fragmentation from repeated kv allocations (mv_alloc churn) rather than raw peak usage.
Anya: Pasting minimal error snippet from the node log:
```
ERROR OOM kv_alloc 0x7f8b2c4e used=11.9GB free=0.3GB slot_frag=0.23
Backtrace: ...
```
Lucas: slot_frag > 0.2 is concerning. Short-term mitigation options: reduce concurrency `max_parallel_requests=2`, force `batch_size=1`, disable prefetch (we already did). Medium-term: enable compact-on-evict and bump slot_compactor aggressiveness.
Sophia: For the quality regression: run an A/B on 500 eval prompts int4 vs int8 (same prompts). If int8 recovers ROUGE, likely quant calibration on attention/kv scales. We should try per-channel scale calibration or fallback int8 for attention/kv only.
Anya: Update from canary: after disabling prefetch and setting max_new_tokens=128, we've run ~2k back-to-back canary inferences with no OOMs. Latency is +8–12ms p50, cost +~8% for this config. Starting int8 comparison now.
Dmitri: Good. If stable, propose rollout plan: keep palomino default as int4 but with `max_new_tokens=128` and `prefetch=false` for first 48h, monitor memory fragmentation and rollback if slot_frag trends up. Then gradually relax limits and enable compact-on-evict.
Lucas: Add an automated eval alert to the pipeline: rollback if ROUGE drops > 1.5 pts on summarization or if OOM rate > 0.1% across the pool.
Anya: Will update the canary config, add the eval A/B, and post numbers tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
